meta.title: Use and Maintenance of Glassware Dryer in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To dry washed laboratory glassware quickly and effectively after washing to ensure it is moisture-free before use in extraction, standardization, and phytochemical analysis experiments.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for drying all categories of washed glassware including beakers, flasks, measuring cylinders, pipettes, and Petri dishes.
procedure: After washing glassware with detergent and rinsing with distilled water, place items inverted on the appropriate pegs of the glassware dryer immediately — do not leave wet glassware standing upright as moisture pools inside.
Arrange glassware with openings facing downward so water drains and air circulates inside the vessel.
Place smaller items (test tubes, centrifuge tubes) in the appropriate tube holder slots.
Pipettes should be placed tip-down in the designated pipette holder section.
For forced-air drying (heated glassware dryer): switch on the blower; set temperature to 60–80°C; allow 30–45 minutes for complete drying.
For ambient air drying: allow 1–2 hours minimum for complete drying at room temperature.
Do not use oven drying for volumetric glassware (measuring cylinders, volumetric flasks, pipettes) — heat causes dimensional changes and invalidates calibration.
After drying, inspect glassware for residual moisture by tilting — if water droplets are visible inside, return to the dryer.
Transfer dry glassware to the storage cupboard immediately — do not leave on the dryer indefinitely as it collects dust.
Clean the glassware dryer pegs and tray monthly with mild detergent to remove mineral deposits and organic residues.
Inspect pegs for damage or missing tips — broken pegs scratch glassware; replace immediately.
precautions: Do not dry volumetric glassware in a heated dryer or oven — heat permanently alters calibration marks.
Do not place hot glassware (just removed from oven or hot plate) directly on plastic-tipped pegs — heat deforms the plastic and the glassware can tip over.
Ensure glassware is stable on the pegs — falling wet glassware causes breakage and cuts.
Do not overcrowd the dryer — inadequate air circulation leaves inner surfaces wet.
Inspect each piece of glassware for cracks before placing on the dryer — cracked glassware should be discarded, not washed and returned.
Replace any corroded or broken pegs promptly — metal corrosion contaminates glassware.
